can_answer: partly: the data can show annual counts of pedestrians injured in police-reported Brooklyn crashes from 2013 onward, but not injury risk per pedestrian trip or population because exposure denominators are absent
metric: annual total number of pedestrians injured, summed from number_of_pedestrians_injured
denominator: none; an annual count across Brooklyn crash records
population: pedestrians recorded as injured in police-reported crashes whose borough is Brooklyn
filters: rows with a missing injury count are not included in the injury sum; none are missing in the checked population
plan_changes: The initial 2013-onward period was restricted to complete years 2013–2025 because 2026 is observed only through June 11; the literal case-sensitive borough filter was normalized because the stored borough label is uppercase BROOKLYN.
data_check: The final 2013–2025 population has 473,801 Brooklyn crash rows. The injury field is nonmissing in all 473,801. Each year 2013–2025 has observations from January 1 through December 31. Brooklyn appears uppercase, so the original exact-case filter would return no rows; the final filter normalizes case and whitespace. The check also found 9,700 candidate rows in partial 2026, observed only through June 11, and these are excluded.
limitations: These are annual counts from police-reported crashes, not pedestrian exposure-adjusted risk; the file has no pedestrian-trip or population denominator. Counts can also change with the volume of reported crashes. The partial 2026 year is excluded.
